title: One thing the app can do, one place it is recorded
lede: A teko is one concept whoever fires it — a practice, a member pressing a button, a schedule, the assistant — and every firing lands in one ledger the community can read. Today it is two: the `action` table and `broadcast_types` both mean "action", nothing outside migration 0254 has ever written an action row, and three call sites deliver without recording a run at all. The practices journey assumes this catalog works; it does not yet.

stepsFrom.projector: the paper reader in the roadmap this app was extracted from (src/modules/paper/steps.ts)
stepsFrom.why: The steps of this journey are the sections of its paper. Nothing is stored here because nothing was ever written here — they are projected out of LaTeX at read time by a program this app is not. This app cannot parse a paper and will not learn how, so it says so rather than showing an empty journey.

vocabulary.means: A catalog entry (fi teko): a behaviour plus its configuration, owned by a community, that can be pointed at and fired. Not the thing a member did to an item — that is the operation. One action whoever fires it: a practice, a member pressing a button, a schedule, the assistant.

The kind an action is — deliver, enforce_rule, moderate, ai_review. A column on the action row, never a category of concept: adding a behaviour must not add anything the member has to learn. It is also bounded — an action decides and performs, it does not rewrite the member's content (gh#1399).

A built-in the platform writes into each community as an ordinary row keyed by system_key, so code can point at a behaviour without pointing at an editable name. Today they are written by migration 0254 and nothing else, so a community founded since has none (gh#1692) — which is why seeding must become application code that runs at provisioning.
